text:
Alex Chen: Heads up — saw a p95 latency spike for tenant 'analytics' on the canary cluster after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. Not sure if this is batching or cache-related.
Samira Patel: Where in the stack? which commit/sha?
Alex Chen: commit f3a9c2b, rollout started at 10:05 UTC. Quick numbers from Grafana: baseline p95 ~ 110ms -> canary p95 ~ 320ms (tokens/sec unchanged). also noticed request tailbacks in queueer.
Maya Ortiz: Any change in KV metrics? eviction counters, mem-usage?
Alex Chen: Yep. KV evictions jumped: kv_cache.evictions_total from ~23/min -> ~420/min on canary nodes. Resident set increased by ~200MB per process.
Raj Singh: What batching params were in effect for the canary? batch_cap / max_delay?
Alex Chen: Using defaults we ship for the rollout: batch_cap=64, max_delay_ms=8, continuous_batching=true.
Simon Liu: The selector change made the scheduler prefer the fast-matmul kernel for medium sequence lengths — that kernel uses a slightly different workspace layout, could increase per-request scratch. If scratch lives near KV memory budget it can cause more evictions under concurrency.
Maya Ortiz: That matches the eviction jump. Can we repro with the replay harness? Multi-tenant vs single-tenant will tell us if it's interaction across tenant memory footprints.
Alex Chen: Replayed a 10-min multi-tenant trace with the canary config. Single-tenant (analytics only) replay showed normal evictions (~10/min). Multi-tenant run reproduced the spike.
Raj Singh: So it's an interference problem (KV pressure + larger kernel scratch). Short experiment: reduce batch_cap to 32 on canary and re-run multi-tenant replay. If p95 drops, we have a knob.
Alex Chen: Starting a quick experiment now. Command I used: `./bin/replay --trace traces/multi_tenant_20260314.json --iterations 1 --conf conf/canary.json` (canary.conf includes kernel selector from f3a9c2b).
deploy-bot: canary rollout f3a9c2b started (10:05 UTC)
perf-bot: scheduled perf job 2026-03-17T11:30Z: replay( multi_tenant_20260314 ) -> queued
Maya Ortiz: Also collect `/proc/meminfo` and `perf top --call-graph` on one hot process during the run. If kernel scratch is the cause we should see increased anonymous mappings and kernel-related symbols dominating.
Samira Patel: If reducing batch_cap fixes it we should consider auto-adjusting batch_cap based on resident memory headroom per-process. But first reproduce and get a flamegraph.
Alex Chen: Quick result: with batch_cap=32 p95 for analytics in the replay dropped to 140ms, evictions fell to ~35/min. With batch_cap=64 p95 ~310ms and evictions ~410/min. I'll attach flamegraph and `smem` diff in the ticket.
Simon Liu: Nice. That implicates the batch sizing interacting with kernel choice. Longer term: either tweak kernel selector (avoid high-scratch kernel for multi-tenant mid-seq workloads) or adapt batch_cap per-tenant/hardware.
Raj Singh: Add an automated apples-to-apples harness run comparing old vs new selector with identical batching and trace seeds. We need to ensure we're not regressing throughput/cost while fixing fairness.
Maya Ortiz: Agreed. Plan: 1) repro + collect flamegraphs (today) 2) run selector A/B with batch_cap fixed at 32 and 64 (tomorrow) 3) test adaptive batch_cap heuristic on a small canary (next week). I'll spin up the replay configs.
Alex Chen: Filing PERF-4189 with logs, sample flamegraph snippet, conf diff, and the exact replay commands.
Samira Patel: Thanks. If anyone is free, please help run step 2 — need a couple of runs to reduce noise.
Raj Singh: I'll take the afternoon slot — will run on the C12 pool.
Maya Ortiz: I'll draft the adaptive proposal after we confirm root cause. For the ticket: add a short checklist for mitigations (hotfix: roll kernel selector back or set batch_cap=32 for affected tenants).
Alex Chen: Added the mitigation note. Will update when I have full artifacts. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: perf job 2026-03-17T11:30Z started
Alex Chen: End of thread — collecting artifacts and will ping when uploaded to PERF-4189.
